firstWord.name: Get a correct word displaying
firstWord.description: The first scenario just expects you to choose the first word from `commonWords()`. That word is `which`. To pass this scenario, you need to guess that word and stop. You can check your wiring is correct before moving onto more complex situations.

handleWrong.name: Handle entirely wrong
handleWrong.description: Nice work on getting that first bit wired up! For this second scenario, you're expected to use two guesses. The first will again be the first word from the array (that's always the case!). That will be totally wrong, so you then need to move onto the next word in the array, which will be right!

handlePartial.name: Handle partially right
handlePartial.description: OK, we've got some momentum. This is where things get more fun. The next few scenarios come back as a mixture of `correct` and `absent` letters. Choose the next best word from the array based on your knowledge of the `correct` and `absent` letters you've found so far.

handlePresent.name: Handle present letters
handlePresent.description: Fantastic! Now the final tricky bit. You need to incorporate `present` letters. Good luck, you've got this!

whereToStart.question: Where do I even start?
whereToStart.answer: Begin by guessing the first word from `commonWords()`. Get the loop that guesses a word and checks the result working before worrying about being smart.

readStates.question: How do I know how my guess did?
readStates.answer: `guess(word)` hands you back an array with one state per letter: `"correct"`, `"present"`, or `"absent"`. That array is the only thing you learn from a guess, so everything you know has to come from it.

rememberLearned.question: How do I remember what I've learned across guesses?
rememberLearned.answer: Keep a knowledge structure outside the loop: the letters known to be absent, the letters known to be in the word somewhere, and per-position the letters you know are NOT there.

pickNextGuess.question: How do I pick the next guess?
pickNextGuess.answer: Filter `commonWords()`: keep only words that have all the correct letters in the right slots, contain every present letter (but not in positions you've ruled out), and contain none of the absent letters. Pick the first match.

whenToStop.question: When do I stop?
whenToStop.answer: Stop as soon as every state comes back `"correct"`, or after `6` guesses. Otherwise you'll keep guessing past the end of the board.

guess.description: Guesses a word. It draws the word on the next row of the board, colors it in, and returns an array with the state of each letter.

commonWords.description: Returns an array of 100+ common five-letter words to use as guesses.

push.description: Adds an element onto the end of an array, changing the array in place.

includes.description: Check whether an array contains an item, or a string contains a substring.

length.description: The number of items in an array, or characters in a string.
